definition: The unit used to measure the amount of substance. One mole contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number).
clues: This is a unit of measurement in chemistry
It represents a specific number of particles
One of these contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles
The unit of amount of substance — one mole of any substance contains Avogadro's number of particles

definition: The number of particles in one mole of a substance: 6.02 × 10²³.
clues: This is a very large number used in chemistry
It tells you how many particles are in one mole
It is approximately 6 × 10²³
The number of atoms, molecules or ions in one mole — 6.02 × 10²³

definition: The sum of the relative atomic masses of all atoms in a formula. Symbol: Mr.
clues: This is a calculated value for a compound
It is found by adding relative atomic masses together
Its symbol is Mr
The sum of the Ar values of all atoms in a chemical formula — used to calculate moles and percentage composition

definition: In a chemical reaction, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products. No atoms are created or destroyed.
clues: This is a fundamental law in chemistry
It applies to every chemical reaction
Mass is neither gained nor lost
The total mass of reactants always equals the total mass of products — atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed

definition: A chemical equation where the number of each type of atom is the same on both sides. Reflects conservation of mass.
clues: This is a type of chemical equation
It has equal numbers of each atom on both sides
It obeys the law of conservation of mass
An equation where the number of each element is the same on both sides — showing that no atoms are lost or gained

definition: The reactant that is completely used up in a reaction, limiting the amount of product that can be made.
clues: This is a term used in chemical reactions
It is the reactant that runs out first
It determines the maximum yield of product
The reactant that is used up entirely — once gone, the reaction stops and no more product can form

definition: The reactant that is present in greater quantity than needed — some is left over when the limiting reactant is used up.
clues: This is a term used in chemical reactions
It is the reactant that is not fully used up
Some of it remains at the end of the reaction
The reactant present in more than enough quantity — a portion is left unreacted when the limiting reactant runs out

definition: The actual yield of a product expressed as a percentage of the theoretical maximum yield. Calculated as: (actual yield ÷ theoretical yield) × 100.
clues: This is a percentage calculated in chemistry
It compares how much product you actually got to the maximum possible
It can never exceed 100%
(actual yield ÷ theoretical yield) × 100 — tells you how efficient a reaction was

definition: The maximum amount of product that could be produced in a reaction, calculated from the amounts of reactants used.
clues: This is the maximum possible amount of product
It is calculated using moles and the balanced equation
It is often not fully achieved in practice
The maximum mass of product predicted from the moles of limiting reactant — rarely achieved in practice due to losses

definition: A measure of how much of the reactants end up as useful product. Calculated as: (mass of desired product ÷ total mass of all products) × 100.
clues: This is a percentage used in green chemistry
It measures how much reactant becomes useful product
A higher value means less waste
(mass of desired product ÷ total mass of all products) × 100 — high values indicate efficient, sustainable reactions

definition: The amount of solute dissolved in a given volume of solution. Measured in mol/dm³ or g/dm³.
clues: This is a property of a solution
It describes how much solute is dissolved per unit volume
It is measured in mol/dm³ or g/dm³
The number of moles or grams of solute per cubic decimetre (litre) of solution

definition: The substance that is dissolved in a solvent to make a solution.
clues: This is a component of a solution
It is the substance that dissolves
Salt is an example when it dissolves in water
The dissolved substance in a solution — e.g. salt (solute) dissolved in water (solvent) forms salt solution

definition: The liquid in which a solute is dissolved to form a solution.
clues: This is a component of a solution
It is the liquid that does the dissolving
Water is the most common example
The liquid in which a solute dissolves — water is the most common solvent

definition: A technique used to find the concentration of an acid or alkali by reacting it with a solution of known concentration until neutralisation.
clues: This is an analytical technique in chemistry
It is used to find the concentration of an acid or alkali
It uses a burette and an indicator
A procedure where a solution of known concentration is added to an unknown concentration until neutralisation — used to calculate the unknown concentration

definition: A piece of laboratory equipment used in titrations to deliver precise, controlled volumes of solution.
clues: This is a piece of lab equipment
It is used in titrations
It can deliver precise volumes of liquid
A long, graduated glass tube with a tap — used to add precise volumes of solution during a titration

definition: A piece of laboratory equipment used to accurately measure and transfer a fixed volume of liquid.
clues: This is a piece of lab equipment
It measures an accurate, fixed volume of liquid
It is used to transfer solutions accurately in titrations
A glass tube used to transfer an exact volume of liquid — e.g. 25.0 cm³ of alkali into a conical flask for titration

definition: The point in a titration when the indicator permanently changes colour, showing that neutralisation is complete.
clues: This is a term used in titrations
It is detected by a colour change
It shows that the reaction is complete
The point in a titration when the indicator changes colour permanently — showing exactly enough acid has been added to neutralise the alkali

definition: A substance that changes colour at different pH values, used to detect the end point of a titration.
clues: This is a substance used in acid-base chemistry
It changes colour depending on pH
It is used to find the end point of a titration
A dye that changes colour at specific pH values — used in titrations to signal when neutralisation is complete

definition: The mass of one mole of a substance, numerically equal to the relative formula mass in grams. Unit: g/mol.
clues: This is the mass of one mole of a substance
It is measured in g/mol
It equals the relative formula mass in grams
The mass of one mole of a substance in grams — numerically the same as the Mr value

definition: At room temperature and pressure, one mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ (24,000 cm³). This allows moles of gases to be calculated from volume.
clues: This is a concept related to gases and moles
One mole of any gas occupies a specific volume at room conditions
The molar volume at RTP is 24 dm³
At room temperature and pressure, one mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³ — used to convert between moles and gas volumes

definition: The volume occupied by one mole of a gas at a given temperature and pressure. At RTP, this is 24 dm³.
clues: This is a term relating gas volume to moles
It is 24 dm³ at room temperature and pressure
It applies to all gases equally
The volume of one mole of gas at RTP — 24 dm³ regardless of which gas, used in gas volume calculations

definition: The percentage by mass of each element in a compound. Calculated using relative atomic masses.
clues: This is a calculation in chemistry
It tells you how much of each element is in a compound
It is expressed as a percentage
(mass of element in 1 mole ÷ relative formula mass) × 100 — tells you the proportion of each element in a compound
